$comment: Probes that fail TODAY, where, how, and the pull request that fixes each (verdict.mjs). The list may only shrink: a listed probe that passes turns its cell red, so the fixing pull request deletes its entry. `when` maps an axis to a value or a list; an entry without `when` matches every run. `failure` is a regex for the expected failure: every failure line of the probe in that run must match it, so a crash, a TypeError or a lost file in a listed probe is still a REGRESSION. Entries and signatures were derived from local runs on Vitest 5 (RNTL 12.9, 13.3 and 14.1, both engines, every runtime combination) except where `why` says otherwise.

entries.failure: ^rntl-auto-cleanup\.test\.tsx: the previous test's tree was unmounted: AssertionError: expected \+0 to be 1
entries.why: RNTL registers cleanup only through a global afterEach. Both engines, every RNTL.

entries.failure: ^rntl-findby-fake-timers\.test\.tsx: findBy advances Vitest's fake timers: Error: Unable to find an element with text: ready
entries.why: RNTL drives fake timers only through a global jest, which only jest-compat defines. Both engines, every RNTL, globals on or off. NOTE: #342 documents this as a limitation (use jest-compat, or advance timers by hand) and does not fix it, so this entry will not go stale when #342 merges; no open pull request fixes it.

entries.failure: ^rntl-nested-text\.test\.tsx: nested Text is queryable by its own text: Error: Unable to find an element with text: inner
entries.why: RCTVirtualText is registered as a text host for RNTL 14 only.

entries.failure: ^(unhandled error \(from recoverable-error\.test\.tsx\): Error: There was an error during concurrent rendering but React was able to recover|the JSON report says success: true, but Vitest exited 1$)
entries.why: react-test-renderer 19 reports a recoverable error through process.emit('uncaughtException'). RNTL 14 renders without it. Both engines.
A synchronous requireActual compiles a second module graph under Node, so the mock's real `read` sees Node's store.

entries.failure: ^partial-mock-store\.test\.ts: \[vitest\] There was an error when mocking a module\.
entries.why: Under the mock engine the factory itself throws (Vitest reports only that mocking failed), a different symptom from the native engine's split store. #345 rewrites requireActual in the factory to vi.importActual for both engines, but that it clears this one is NOT yet observed.

entries.failure: ^aliased-sibling-string\.test\.ts: .*: AssertionError: expected null to be 'written by the test'
entries.why: The sibling's directory is externalized, so Node loads the aliased source and its own store. Observed to pass with jest-compat on, whose Node-side resolution reaches the same copy.
Node's alias fallback cannot represent a regex alias: Cannot find module.
Node compiles the aliased source to CommonJS: Cannot use 'import.meta' outside a module.

entries.failure: ^esm-default-interop\.test\.ts: .*: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined \(reading '__extends'\)
entries.why: Babel's interopRequireDefault reads exports.default from __esModule CommonJS.

entries.failure: ^jest-fake-timer-options\.test\.ts: .*: AssertionError: expected 'the fake clock stood still' to be 'fired'
entries.why: jest.useFakeTimers passes Jest's options to Vitest, which drops advanceTimers. Both engines.

entries.failure: ^jest-error-equality\.test\.ts: .*: AssertionError: expected Error: bad input .* to deeply equal Error: bad input
entries.why: Vitest compares Errors' own enumerable properties, per-instance methods included. Both engines.

entries.failure: ^the banner does not name the safeAreaContext preset: \[vitest-native\] engine: (native|mock)
entries.why: The banner names no presets. Both engines.

entries.failure: ^hot-automock-[ab]\.test\.ts: gets its own factory, and an automock for the module it automocks: AssertionError: expected false to be true
entries.why: NOT observed locally (no Vitest 4 on this machine): from #338, which reproduced it on Vitest 4.1.11. Vitest 4.1 replays a remembered factory from a placeholder node the hot runtime keeps across files; Vitest 5 is unaffected.
